subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics, Year 10
placeName: Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia, Tasmania, Australian Capital Territory and Northern Territory

points.title: Exact values and approximations
points.brief: An exact value, such as √2 or π, is kept as it is, while a decimal such as 1.414 is only an approximation of it.

points.title: Rounding errors in repeated calculations
points.brief: Rounding early and then using the rounded value again and again lets small errors build up, so round only at the end.

points.title: How measurement errors affect results
points.brief: An error in a measured length grows when it is used in a calculation, so a small error in a side length makes a larger error in an area or volume.

points.title: Simplifying with the index laws
points.brief: Simplifying expressions that combine products, quotients and powers of variables, with positive and negative indices, such as (2x³y)² ÷ 4xy = x⁵y.

points.title: Expanding and factorising as reverse processes
points.brief: Factorising undoes expanding, so a factorised answer can be checked by expanding it, as with x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3).

points.title: Completing the square
points.brief: A monic quadratic can be written in completed square form by adding and taking away the square of half the coefficient of x, so x² + 6x + 2 = (x + 3)² − 7.

points.title: Equations with algebraic fractions
points.brief: Multiply every term by the lowest common denominator to clear the fractions, then solve, so x/3 + x/4 = 7 gives x = 12.

points.title: Solving linear inequalities
points.brief: Inequalities are solved like equations, except the sign flips when both sides are multiplied or divided by a negative number, so −2x < 6 gives x > −3.

points.title: Inequalities on the Cartesian plane
points.brief: An inequality such as y > 2x + 1 is a region on one side of a line, and a test point such as (0, 0) shows which side to shade.

points.title: Simultaneous equations by graphing
points.brief: The solution of two linear equations is the point where their lines cross, which makes both equations true.

points.title: Simultaneous equations by substitution
points.brief: Rearrange one equation for one variable, substitute it into the other, solve, then substitute back to find the second variable.

points.title: Simultaneous equations by elimination
points.brief: Add or subtract the equations, after multiplying if needed, so that one variable cancels out, then solve for the other.

points.title: Exponential growth and decay graphs
points.brief: A graph of y = aˣ curves upward ever faster when a is above 1 (growth) and falls towards zero when a is between 0 and 1 (decay).

points.title: Solving simple exponential equations
points.brief: Write both sides as powers of the same base, then set the indices equal, so 2ˣ = 32 = 2⁵ gives x = 5.

points.title: Compound interest
points.brief: Compound interest earns interest on interest, so an amount grows by the same factor each period, A = P(1 + r)ⁿ.

points.title: Depreciation
points.brief: An item that loses a fixed percentage of its value each year shrinks by the same factor each year, such as 0.85 for 15% depreciation.

points.title: Choosing a linear, quadratic or exponential model
points.brief: Equal differences each step suggest a linear model, equal ratios each step suggest an exponential model, and a rise then fall suggests a quadratic.

points.title: Volume of composite solids
points.brief: A composite solid built from prisms and cylinders has a volume found by adding, or subtracting, the volumes of its parts.

points.title: Surface area of composite solids
points.brief: The surface area of a composite solid counts only the faces on the outside, leaving out any faces where parts join.

points.title: Logarithmic scales
points.brief: On a logarithmic scale each equal step multiplies the quantity, often by 10, as on the Richter and decibel scales.

points.title: Scaling length, area and volume
points.brief: If lengths are multiplied by a scale factor k, area is multiplied by k² and volume by k³.

points.title: Angles of elevation and depression
points.brief: The angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal to an object, and the angle of depression down from the horizontal, and both are used with trigonometry.

points.title: True bearings
points.brief: A true bearing gives a direction as a three-figure angle measured clockwise from north, such as 045° for north-east.

points.title: Problems with two right-angled triangles
points.brief: Some problems need two right-angled triangles, using a side found in the first to solve the second, such as the height of a building seen from two points.

points.title: Demonstration and proof
points.brief: A demonstration shows something is true in one case, while a proof uses logical steps from known facts to show it is always true.

points.title: Proving triangles congruent
points.brief: A congruence proof names the matching sides and angles with reasons, then states the test used, such as SAS.

points.title: Proofs with angle properties
points.brief: Known angle facts, such as angles in a triangle and angles on parallel lines, are chained with reasons to prove a new result.

points.title: Networks, vertices and edges
points.brief: A network uses vertices (points) and edges (lines) to show connections, such as towns joined by roads, and a vertex's degree is the number of edges it meets.

points.title: Connected networks and paths
points.brief: A network is connected if every vertex can be reached from every other, and the degrees of the vertices decide whether a path can use every edge exactly once.

points.title: Questioning statistical claims
points.brief: A media claim needs checking for who collected the data, how big and how fair the sample was, and whether the conclusion goes further than the data.

points.title: Five-number summary and interquartile range
points.brief: The five-number summary is the minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum, and the interquartile range is upper quartile minus lower quartile.

points.title: Box plots
points.brief: A box plot draws the five-number summary, and placing two box plots on one scale compares the centre, spread and shape of two data sets.

points.title: Scatterplots and association
points.brief: A scatterplot shows two numerical variables, and its pattern shows whether their association is positive or negative, strong or weak, and linear or not.

points.title: Two-way tables for categorical data
points.brief: A two-way table counts two categorical variables together, and comparing row or column percentages shows whether they may be related.

points.title: The language of conditional probability
points.brief: Words such as given, if, then and knowing that signal conditional probability, the chance of one event when another is known to have happened.

points.title: Conditional probability from a two-way table
points.brief: To find a probability given a condition, use only the row or column for that condition as the total.

points.title: Conditional probability from a tree diagram
points.brief: In a tree diagram without replacement, the second branches show probabilities given the first outcome, and multiplying along a path gives the combined probability.

points.title: Independent and dependent events
points.brief: Events are independent if one does not change the chance of the other, such as two coin tosses, and dependent if it does, such as drawing cards without replacement.
